The cashier Anthony denied me the purchase of female betta fish that I kindly explained and showed him I had a sorority tank for. I recently had an angelfish that killed all my female betta fish and was feeling down about it and wanted to restock some after I had removed the angelfish. Anthony continued to argue with me that I couldn't keep multiple (6) female fish because they were going to fight, which I continued to tell him they do not and that I had experience with them.i explained to him that he was wrong and had the wrong info about female betta fish. I understand the abuse of some pet owners, but this is definitely not the case here. I had to leave the store very upset and with tears in my eyes because of the fish that I had picked out excitedly and had to leave behind. I will not be getting my fish from here anymore, unfortunately.

I had a very disappointing experience at this Petco location due to the conduct of the store manager, Daniel.

I came in to return some items totaling about $150. Per Petco’s return policy, items can be returned to any location and must be refunded using the original form of payment. Since the return exceeded a certain amount, it required manager approval.

Daniel arrived and asked why I was returning the items. I explained that I found them cheaper elsewhere. He immediately demanded to see the physical card used for the purchase. I informed him that I used Apple Pay, which is considered the original form of payment according to Petco's own policy.

Despite this, Daniel insisted he couldn’t process the return without a physical card. I asked, “Are you saying you suspect fraud?” to which he smiled and said, “Yes.” This interaction felt less about policy and more about exerting authority. I returned home and I did my due diligence, called Petco corporate, and confirmed that the return could be processed using Apple Pay.

After calling corporate I returned to the store to attempt the refund once more. In addition, to ease his concerns and in accordance with Petco policy—which allows ID scanning when fraud is suspected—I offered to show my driver's license. I had no issue with this if it meant the return could be completed. However, instead of accepting that or verifying with corporate, Daniel claimed that individual stores can have their own return policies. I asked to see this supposed store-specific policy, and after going to the back, he returned and admitted they had no written copy. He then pulled up the general Petco return policy on his phone—which, notably, did not say anything about requiring a physical card, only that the return must be made to the original form of payment.

Seeing that the policy didn’t support his claim, he shifted focus to a clause stating that “Petco can limit returns.” He used this line to deny my return altogether. At this point, it felt more about maintaining control than following procedure. His tone and attitude were dismissive, and despite my efforts to stay calm and respectful, I felt profiled and unwelcome.

For comparison, I went to the College Point Petco location afterward. The manager there was courteous and professional. She processed my return using Apple Pay within five minutes—no issues, no attitude.

The contrast between these two experiences was stark. While the College Point team upheld Petco’s values and policy, Daniel at this location seemed more interested in asserting his authority than helping a customer. I sincerely hope this feedback is used to provide him with the training he clearly needs—on both customer service and company policy.

I’ve taken my senior dog, Malia, to Petco grooming locations before (including in Chicago), and I’ve never encountered anything as needlessly difficult or rude as what I experienced here.

I came all the way from Scarsdale to Forest Hills after a long day at work, and spent nearly an extra hour scrambling to meet this guy’s ever-changing demands. The groomer I dealt with seemed determined from the start to find a reason not to groom my dog. First, he demanded not just rabies vaccine documentation (which is standard), but an actual signed veterinary certificate—something no other Petco has ever required. Fine. I made multiple calls to my vet and got him what he wanted. Then he said the Bordetella and parvo vaccines were a problem because my original record was “just a receipt.” I again jumped through hoops and provided an official expiration record from my vet’s app.

Even after all that, instead of moving forward, he started grilling me about whether my dog had ever had seizures. I told him that yes, she did many years ago, but she hasn’t had any in a long time and was cleared by a vet. That still wasn’t good enough—he then demanded proof she was cleared of seizures, something I obviously don’t have nearly a decade later. It was a ridiculous and frankly insulting exchange. He acted like I was trying to sneak in a dangerous animal instead of bring in a well-behaved senior dog with a clean track record.

And after all that, instead of trying to work with me, he smugly suggested I just buy Petco grooming supplies and do it myself. As if that was some kind of helpful solution. Yes, I know I can groom my dog myself—but that’s why I came to a professional in the first place, after a long day and long drive. His tone made it feel more like a dismissal than a suggestion.

It was clear he didn’t want to do the grooming and was looking for any excuse to say no. He showed no flexibility, no warmth, and no interest in helping solve the issue. Just a brick wall of attitude and red tape.

If you’re considering this Petco location for grooming—don’t. Go anywhere else. This was hands down the worst customer service experience I’ve ever had at a Petco, and it left me incredibly frustrated after spending so much time trying to do the right thing.
